newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-WEEK AHEAD-Australian markets await jobs data.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-WEEK AHEAD-Australian markets await jobs data.

text.p: Australian markets are expected to start the week on an upbeat note after U.S. markets reacted favourably to the keenly awaited August payrolls data on Friday.
Markets worldwide had been bracing for the data, with the strength shown in the August report seen as a key determinant in how much the Federal Reserve would need to raise interest rates.

The 250,000 rise in August employment levels, almost spot on the median forecast of a 244,00 rise, still left markets factoring in a modest 25 basis point tightening in U.S. rates, but eased concerns that the Fed would have to aggressively hike rates by at least 50 basis points.

Local markets will still be focusing on the U.S. this week for clues on the rates outlook, with the release of the August producer price index on Thursday and August retail sales and consumer prices on Friday.
Thursday is also a big day for domestic data with the release of August employment figures.
Economists expect a modest rise of 12,000 jobs for the month, not enough to shift the jobless rate from 8.5 percent.
Movement, or rather the lack of it, in the unemployment rate is being keenly watched given that the Reserve Bank gave it such a high profile when it eased policy in July.
Hopes of a further cut were dented last week by a sharp jump in July retail sales and by retiring RBA governor Bernie Fraser who said there was little need for early monetary policy action.
However, Fraser did say in a speech in Tokyo last Thursday that policy was constantly under review, with the particular regard to employment, wages growth and business investment.

A rise in unemployment in the August data, which some economists see as high as 8.7 percent against 8.5 percent in July, could see the market quickly putting a case for a policy easing before the year-end back on the agenda.

"Given the RBA's continuing publicly-stated concerns about the level of joblessness at present, a flat to negative employment result in August would heighten specualtion that the RBA will move to easy policy settings again in late 1996," Westpac senior economist John Peters said.
Fraser, who finishes up at Martin Place on September 17, will be appearing before a parliamentary committee on Thursday with his replacement, current Deputy Governor Ian Macfarlane.
While they will be answering questions on the RBA's annual report, traders will be listening for any policy clues.
On Monday, the ANZ job ads series should provide some clues as to what the labour market will look like into early 1997.
July housing finance data on Tuesday is expected to show a reasonable rise, but economists said that after two consecutive monthly falls housing is yet to move fully into recovery.
BONDS (Fri: 10 year bonds 8.22 pct, 3 year 7.43 pct)

Australian bonds will start the week on a buoyant note, after rallying in SYCOM trading on the U.S. jobs data. The fact that only a modest rate hike was now expected helped the U.S. market and saw the local bond futures rally across the curve.
Both the three and 10-year September contracts closed SYCOM six points above their Friday floor close, with December bank bill contracts gaining five points in the night session.

While the market will be watching what happens in Treasuries, the main event locally will be Australia's own labour force report on Thursday with any signs of weakness expected to see bonds rally on rate cut expectations.
Bond yields rose last week amid aggressive liquidation in the run up to the U.S. data and amid disappointment that the RBA did not ease policy again.
"Despite a modest rise in yields, bonds remain moderately expensive," said AMP Investments in its weekly outlook.

"While a soft economy and continued good news on inflation should support bonds in the short term, our indicators suggest much of this good news is already reflected in current yields. The broader trend is expected to be bearish from here," it said.
AUSTRALIAN DOLLAR (Fri: 0.7936/41, New York US$0.7990/95)
The Australian dollar will open the week about half a centy under its 1996 high, after rallying again in offshore trade on Friday and finishing one cent up on the week.
The May 1996 high of US$0.8050 could be targetted this week if the offshore interest remains and the AUD can establish a solid foothold above $0.8000, traders said.
The Aussie was also firmer against the yen, moving above the 87 yen level for the first time since mid-July.

The AUD benefitted on Friday, as it did on Thursday, from the offshore interpretation of Fraser's remarks in Tokyo that monetary policy would be held steady, and the perception that U.S. rates would now only need to rise modestly.
Higher oil prices and concerns over supply are also seen as supprtive of the AUD this week.
However, if Thursday's employment report is weak, the dollar may come under some pressure on speculation of a local rate cut. AUSTRALIAN STOCKS (Fri: All Ordinaries 2237.0, down 20.4)
The outlook for Australian shares remains mixed to weaker.
Near term sentiment was seen subject to Wall Street and U.S. bond market reaction to economic data which was prompting tightening fears.
On Friday the Dow Jones Industrial Average reacted favourably to the payrolls data, rising 52.9 points to 5659.86.
Last week the benchmark All Ordinaries fell 31.7 points or 1.4 percent.
"The market is fairly fragile at the moment, volumes have been light and the index choppy.It's hard to pick a strong lead," said Derek Bond, a dealer at brokerage Burrel and Co.

Bond said one focus for the market was commodity prices with the market concerned about the continuing weakness of copper prices. There was also disappointed that the price of gold did not react to the Gulf crisis last week.
"Gold looks like its stuck in a range between US$380 to US$390 in the near term," Bond said.
The week ahead is the last of the current reporting season and typically sees more underperforming firms release results.

Results due include Bank of Melbourne, Seven Network Ltd, Hudson Conway Ltd, Santos Ltd, all on Monday; Davids Ltd, GIO Australia Ltd (Tuesday); Village Roadshow Ltd, Delta Gold NL (Wednesday); RTZ-CRA Ltd, Gibson Chemical Industries Ltd, AIDC Ltd (Thursday); and Australis Media Ltd, David Jones Ltd, Pacific Dunlop Ltd (Friday).
